item.title: Attorney General issues unusual statement: No one will be investigated without evidence
item.description:
Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara clarified that citizens and elected officials cannot be investigated without evidence justifying such an investigation.
"If the Shin Bet or any other body possesses evidence warranting an investigation, it is welcome to present it. Anyone who needs to be investigated will be investigated," a statement issued on her behalf said.
The statement also alleged that the Shin Bet has failed for two days to transfer the evidence it collected to the special investigative team established on the recommendation of Justice Sohlberg, in cooperation with the police and under the supervision of the State Attorney's Office, thereby delaying the investigation.

item.title: High Court issues unusual ruling: Prison sentence suspended
item.description: The High Court has ruled that the young man convicted of killing Aisha al-Rabi in 2018 will not begin serving his prison sentence until his appeal has been decided.

item.title: 60% of Israelis support unity government, 74% oppose coalition relying on Arab parties
item.description: Only 34% of the public prefer another round of elections, while 74% oppose a minority government led by Gadi Eisenkot and relying on Arab parties.

item.title: MK Moshe Saada says chances of forming a government with Arab parties and haredim are zero

item.title: 3,500 Hezbollah terrorist sites destroyed in eight months
item.description: After eight months of operations in the Wadi Saluki, Qantara, and Litani areas, troops from the IDF's 7th Brigade have completed their mission in southern Lebanon.

item.title: The mystery of the 200,000 double envelopes solved
item.description: The Election Committee expected 650,000 double-envelope votes, but counted only 451,000 due to a last-minute IDF decision.

item.title: Channel 12: Bullets strike homes and vehicles in Nevatim, residents report
item.description:
Residents of Nevatim in southern Israel reported bullet impacts on the walls of their homes and on vehicles near a playground, following reports of gunfire in the area, Channel 12 News correspondent Itay Gal-On reported.
"I came back from shopping and saw a bullet hole," said Alex, a local resident. "A week or two ago, there was heavy gunfire in the surrounding communities. Unfortunately, that's nothing new. Then I heard a very loud bang, and apparently this is what happened. We need an Iron Dome here in our community."

item.title: Iran rejects US proposal
item.description:
The Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, stated that the United States' response regarding Iran's rights and demands was unconvincing.
He said that the United States must provide a full, clear, and explicit response to all seven conditions set by Iran.

item.title: Disturbing footage: Forklift driver runs over coworker, killing him
item.description: A 26-year-old man has been charged with fatally running over his coworker at a factory in northern Israel while operating a forklift without a license and under the influence of alcohol. The incident was caught on camera.

item.description: The Torah’s prohibitions assume our capacity for self-control. Hashem emphasized this: “Sin lies at the doorway…but you can control it."

item.title: Religious Zionism to recommend Netanyahu and call for a broad Jewish government
item.description: The Religious Zionism party announced that it will recommend Benjamin Netanyahu to form the next government tomorrow and call for an end to the boycotts imposed by left-wing parties.

item.title: Yechiel Jacobs: Fighting Antisemitism with humor, despite death threats
item.description: In a conversation at the i24NEWS studios, comedian and pro-Israel activist Yechiel Jacobs revealed the threats against his family, the unexpected success of his videos, and why he believes humor can reach audiences traditional advocacy cannot.

item.title: Military correspondent: 'Trump announcement not a big surprise'
item.description: Military correspondent Doron Kadosh says President Trump appears to be accelerating plans to end decades of US military aid to Israel; but this does not come as a big surprise.'

item.title: Following Draft Law statement, Shas decides to recommend Netanyahu
item.description: Shas's Council of Torah Sages has decided to recommend Benjamin Netanyahu to President Isaac Herzog as its candidate to form the next government.

item.title: Analysis: Trump's announcement shows that cutting aid to Israel is popular in US
item.description:
Channel 13 diplomatic correspondent Moriah Asraf warned that the timing of US President Donald Trump's announcement of the end of aid to Israel is a worrying sign of how Israel's standing in the US has fallen.
"What is more troubling than the move itself, which, as noted, was coordinated with Israel, is the fact that Trump is saying this on the eve of the midterm elections. In other words, it's popular," Asraf said. "This paints a troubling and worrying picture of Israel's standing."

item.title: In His Own Words: What El-Sayed says about Israel, Hamas, Iran and the Brotherhood
item.description: The questions he has never answered, essays he pulled from public view, a deleted 9/11 post, three refusals to say Israel has a right to exist, a refusal to name the IRGC to an Iranian-American whose family it hunted, and a 2011 defense of the Brotherhood he has never retracted. Report.

item.title: Former El-Sayed campaign worker indicted over antisemitic campaign targeting Michigan Jews
item.description: Federal prosecutors accuse 12 anti-Israel activists, including a former worker on Abdul El-Sayed’s Senate campaign, of terrorizing Michigan’s Jewish community, vandalizing homes, throwing chemical-filled jars and issuing threats.

item.title: Trump: I reached deal with Netanyahu to stop $4 billion Israel aid
item.description:
US President Donald Trump said today in an interview with Fox News: "Netanyahu and I agreed that we would give Israel $4 billion a year, and we made a deal months ago that we would stop paying them, and they are fine with that - they don't need us. We will not pay Israel any more."
